stops.note: 'leaven', the yeast that makes bread rise
the physiologist Wilhelm Kühne of Heidelberg coined it in 1877 from Greek en zymē, 'in yeast', for ferments working outside living cells
Eduard Buchner's 1897 proof that yeast juice without living cells still ferments sugar won him the 1907 Nobel Prize

current_meaning: a protein that speeds up a chemical reaction in living things
